newsitem.title: ISRAEL: SOCCER-ISRAEL DROP FIVE FOR BREAKING CURFEW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ISRAEL DROP FIVE FOR BREAKING CURFEW.

text.p: Five players were axed from Israel's 20-strong on Tuesday for breaking a team curfew ahead of a World Cup qualifier against Cyprus.

The five -- four first-choice players and a former captain -- had gone to the cinema without informing coach Shlomo Scharf. They failed to return to the team's hotel in time for the curfew, squad officials said.
"I feel betrayed by these players. After having discussed discipline with the team, they went and broke the rules," Scharf told Israel Television.

The axed players were midfielders Haim Revivo of Spanish side Celta Vigo, Avi Nimni of Maccabi Tel Aviv, left-back Felix Halfon of Hapoel Tel Aviv and right-back David Amsalem of league leaders Betar Jerusalem.
The fifth, Nir Klinger, a former captain who plays for Maccabi Tel Aviv, had not been expected to start the match.

Klinger decided to quit international soccer after Sharf's decision. "This is very severe punishment, particularly on the younger players. As for me, I had already made up my mind to quit," said Klinger, capped a record 83 times.
With Tottenham's Ronnie Rosenthal also ruled out after an injury during training on Monday, Israel will take on a drastic new look for Wednesday's tie in Tel Aviv.
"We went to see a movie. It's a kind of therapy for us. We didn't go out to have a good time or to a disco. It looks like the situation is irreversible -- what a pity," Klinger told Israel Radio.
"It was all just a big misunderstanding, but perhaps our mistake was that we did not inform the coach," Nimni said.
Scharf immediately drafted in three players -- internationals Reuven Atar and Avishai Janno of Maccabi Haifa and Shai Holtzman of Hapoel Beersheba.
Team (probable): Rafi Cohen, Alon Harazi or Avishai Janno, Moshe Glam, Amir Shelah, Arik Bennado, Alon Hazan, Tal Banin (captain), Itzik Zohar, Eyal Berkovic, Eli Ohana, Alon Mizrahi
